faults.quote: The day before today.
faults.why: Adverb defined as a noun phrase instead of an adverbial time expression.

notes: أَمْسِ is an indeclinable adverb that always ends in a kasrah (-i); with the definite article, الأَمْسُ is an ordinary noun that declines.

senses.definition: On the day before today.

examples.text: وَصَلْتُ أَمْسِ.
examples.translation: I arrived yesterday.

faults.quote: آكُلُ فََاكِهَةً طَازِجَةً كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
faults.why: Contains a double fatha (فََاكِهَةً) on the first letter of the word.

notes: فَاكِهَة is a mass noun, like English 'fruit'; one piece of fruit is حَبَّةُ فَاكِهَةٍ. The broken plural فَوَاكِه (fawākih) means various kinds of fruit.

senses.definition: The sweet and fleshy part of a plant that contains seeds and is eaten as food.

examples.text: آكُلُ فَاكِهَةً طَازِجَةً كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
examples.translation: I eat fresh fruit every day.

faults.quote: Can sometimes carry a negative connotation of poor quality
faults.why: Restates sense 1.

faults.quote: Αγοράσαμε ένα φτηνό κινητό που χάλασε αμέσως.
faults.why: A cheap phone that broke still primarily means 'inexpensive' (sense 0).

notes: Also spelled φθηνός, the more formal spelling; both are standard.

senses.definition: Costing little money; low in price.

examples.text: Αυτό το φόρεμα είναι πολύ φτηνό.
examples.translation: This dress is very cheap.

senses.definition: Of low quality or little worth.

examples.text: Δεν μου αρέσουν τα φτηνά αστεία.
examples.translation: I don't like cheap jokes.

faults.quote: here; now; in this respect
faults.why: Lists meanings ('now; in this respect') not present in the senses.

faults.quote: Used to indicate the place where the speaker is
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of the word.

notes: With a time expression, εδώ και means 'for ... now': Εδώ και δύο χρόνια μένω στην Αθήνα (I have been living in Athens for two years).

senses.definition: In or to this place, where the speaker is.

examples.text: Είμαι εδώ.
examples.translation: I am here.

faults.quote: Κοιτάχτηκε στον καθρέφτης για να ισιώσει τα μαλλιά του.
faults.why: Ungrammatical case: after 'στον' the accusative 'καθρέφτη' is required, not nominative 'καθρέφτης'.

faults.quote: /kaˈθrefti.s/
faults.why: Misplaced syllable boundary dot before the final consonant /s/.

notes: Also written ο καθρέπτης, a more formal spelling of the same word.

senses.definition: A piece of glass that reflects images.

examples.text: Κοιτάχτηκε στον καθρέφτη για να φτιάξει τα μαλλιά του.
examples.translation: He looked in the mirror to fix his hair.

faults.quote: In Greek, the definite article 'ο' is an integral part
faults.why: Generic grammar rule applying to all Greek nouns, not specific to this word.

notes: The plural is οι ελέφαντες, with the stress on the same syllable as in the singular.

senses.definition: A very large grey mammal with a long trunk, big ears, and tusks, native to Africa and Asia.

faults.quote: Refers specifically to a school student or learner
faults.why: Restates sense 0; can be merged with note 1 and feminine form added.

faults.quote: (philosophy) A person who follows the teachings, philosophy, or method
faults.why: Historical/philosophical sense ('disciple') is not needed at A2.

faults.quote: The philosopher was discussing with his disciples in the courtyard.
faults.why: Ungrammatical in English ('discussing' is transitive and cannot take 'with' alone).

notes: Used for school pupils (primary or secondary) or anyone taking lessons from a teacher; for a university student, use ο φοιτητής / η φοιτήτρια.
The feminine is η μαθήτρια.

senses.definition: A person who goes to school or takes lessons from a teacher.

examples.text: Ο μαθητής διαβάζει το βιβλίο του για το μάθημα.
examples.translation: The student is reading his book for the lesson.

faults.quote: to swim; to wade through
faults.why: 'to wade through' is not in the senses and is not what 'κολυμπώ' means.

faults.quote: To be completely surrounded by or immersed in a liquid.
faults.why: Figurative/colloquial shade ('swimming in oil') is marginal for A2; keep the entry focused on swimming.

notes: Two present forms are both standard: κολυμπώ, and the more everyday κολυμπάω. The past tense is κολύμπησα (I swam).

senses.definition: To move through water by using your arms and legs.

examples.text: Μου αρέσει να κολυμπώ στη θάλασσα το καλοκαίρι.
examples.translation: I like to swim in the sea in the summer.

faults.quote: En inglés se usa 'think' tanto para el proceso mental de pensar
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses while omitting the irregular past form 'thought'.

notes: Verbo irregular: el pasado y el participio son 'thought'.
A diferencia del español, en oraciones negativas es muy común decir 'I don't think that...' para expresar 'creo que no...'.

senses.definition: Usar la mente para reflexionar, razonar o considerar algo.

examples.text: Give me a minute to think about it.
examples.translation: Dame un minuto para pensarlo.

senses.definition: Tener una opinión o creencia sobre algo o alguien.

examples.text: I think this movie is really good.
examples.translation: Creo que esta película es muy buena.

faults.why: Missing the irregular past tense ('threw') and past participle ('thrown').

faults.quote: Hacer caer a alguien al suelo con violencia o fuerza.
faults.why: Throwing someone/something to the ground is just a sub-case of sense 0.

notes: Verbo irregular: el pasado es 'threw' y el participio, 'thrown'.
A diferencia de 'drop' (dejar caer algo), 'throw' implica impulsar el objeto con fuerza por el aire.

senses.definition: Impulsar algo con la mano o con fuerza para que se mueva por el aire o caiga.

examples.text: Throw the ball to me, please.
examples.translation: Lánzame la pelota, por favor.

senses.definition: Organizar o dar una fiesta o celebración.

examples.text: We want to throw a party for her birthday.
examples.translation: Queremos organizar una fiesta para su cumpleaños.

notes: 방 is one room; the whole house or home is 집. It also forms the names of rooms and shops, such as 공부방 (study room) and 노래방 (karaoke room).

senses.definition: A space within a building enclosed by walls and a door.

examples.text: 제 방은 작지만 아주 따뜻해요.
examples.translation: My room is small, but very warm.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense 'you're welcome' (in response to 'dziękuję').

faults.quote: This is the most essential word for polite interaction in Polish.
faults.why: Pure filler; notes[2] also repeats sense 1's gloss.

corrected.shortGloss: please; here you are; you're welcome; pardon
notes: Literally 'I ask', the first-person form of the verb prosić (to ask), used as a fixed polite word.

senses.definition: Used to politely ask for something, or to invite someone to do something, such as come in or sit down.

examples.text: Proszę wejść.
examples.translation: Please come in.

senses.definition: Used when handing or offering something to someone.

examples.text: Proszę, to pana klucz.
examples.translation: Here you are, this is your key.

senses.definition: Used as a polite reply when someone thanks you.

examples.text: Dziękuję za pomoc. — Proszę bardzo!
examples.translation: Thank you for your help. — You're welcome!

senses.definition: Used with rising intonation to ask someone to repeat what they said.

examples.text: Proszę? Nie usłyszałem.
examples.translation: Pardon? I didn't hear.

faults.quote: Used for carrying clothes and personal items when traveling.
faults.why: Repeats the definition word for word.

notes: To pack a suitcase is собирать чемодан (perfective собрать); to unpack it is разбирать (perfective разобрать).

senses.definition: A large rectangular case with a handle for carrying clothes and belongings when travelling.

examples.text: Я кладу платье и рубашку в чемодан.
examples.translation: I am putting a dress and a shirt into the suitcase.

faults.quote: ดี is one of the most common adjectives in Thai
faults.why: Pure filler restating the glosses.

faults.quote: In good health or recovered from an illness.
faults.why: 'Recovered/better' in the example comes from ดีขึ้น, not ดี alone; missing core 'kind/nice' sense.

notes: After a verb it means 'well' (พูดดี, to speak well), and ดีขึ้น (dii khûen) means 'better', as in feeling better.

senses.definition: Of high quality, pleasant, or satisfactory.

examples.text: วันนี้อากาศดีมาก
examples.translation: The weather is very good today.

senses.definition: Of a person or their behavior: kind, friendly, or morally good.

examples.text: เขาเป็นคนดีมาก
examples.translation: He is a very good person.

faults.quote: หลัง is primarily used for the physical back of the human body
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given in the entry.
Should mention its very common A1/A2 use as the classifier for houses.

notes: Often preceded by ข้าง or ด้าน (ข้างหลัง, ด้านหลัง) when referring to the area behind something.
หลัง is also the classifier for houses and buildings (e.g., บ้านสองหลัง 'two houses') and a preposition meaning 'after' in time.

senses.definition: The rear part of the human or animal body, from the neck to the hips.

examples.text: ฉันปวดหลังมากเพราะนั่งทำงานทั้งวัน
examples.translation: My back hurts a lot because I sat working all day.

senses.definition: The area or position at the rear of an object or place.

examples.text: ร้านค้าอยู่หลังบ้านฉัน
examples.translation: The shop is behind my house.

faults.why: Missing crucial stem-consonant mutation warning (p -> b before vowels: cebim, cebi) while note[0] repeats sense[1].

faults.quote: In modern Turkish, 'cep' is also used as a short form for
faults.why: Just repeats sense 1 while omitting the essential p -> b consonant mutation rule.

notes: The final 'p' softens to 'b' before a suffix starting with a vowel: cep → cebi (his/her pocket), cebimde (in my pocket).
In the sense of 'mobile phone', it is a colloquial shortening of 'cep telefonu'.

senses.definition: A small pouch sewn into or onto clothing for carrying small items.

examples.text: Anahtarlarımı cebimde unuttum.
examples.translation: I left my keys in my pocket.

senses.definition: (informal) A mobile phone.

examples.text: Cebimi evde unutmuşum.
examples.translation: I left my mobile phone at home.

faults.quote: Bu kitap çok ilginç bir roman.
faults.why: Example uses zero copula, does not contain any form of 'olmak'.

faults.quote: Ben evdeyim.
faults.why: Example uses the copula suffix (-yim), not the verb 'olmak'.
Senses 2 and 3 artificially split 'to be' and explain English 'be' rather than 'olmak'.
Missing the everyday sense 'to be alright / suitable / ready' (e.g., Oldu!).

corrected.shortGloss: to become; to happen; to be
notes: In the simple present, 'am/is/are' is normally expressed by personal suffixes (like Evdeyim 'I am at home'), not by olmak. Olmak is used for 'to be' when a full verb form is needed (future, conditional, infinitive, etc.).
Also forms countless compound verbs with nouns and adjectives, such as mutlu olmak (to be or get happy) and yardımcı olmak (to help).

senses.definition: To come to be something or enter a new state; to turn into.

examples.text: Büyüyünce doktor olmak istiyorum.
examples.translation: I want to become a doctor when I grow up.

senses.definition: To take place or occur.

examples.text: Dün akşam ne oldu?
examples.translation: What happened last night?

senses.definition: To exist or be in a place, state, or condition (especially in the future, conditional, or infinitive).

examples.text: Yarın saat üçte evde olacağım.
examples.translation: I will be at home tomorrow at three o'clock.

senses.definition: To be ready, suitable, acceptable, or done.

examples.text: Yemek oldu, sofraya gelin.
examples.translation: The food is ready, come to the table.

faults.quote: in Mexico and other regions you will also often hear 'arreglar'
faults.why: In Mexico arreglar is the everyday word; reparar sounds formal or technical.
The 'notice' sense needs its preposition: reparar en algo.

notes: In everyday Mexican Spanish, arreglar is the usual word for fixing something; reparar sounds more formal or technical, as at a repair shop.
In the sense 'notice' it always takes en (reparar en algo) and is formal; in speech people say fijarse en or darse cuenta de.

senses.definition: To make something that was broken or damaged work again.

examples.text: Necesito reparar mi computadora porque no enciende.
examples.translation: I need to repair my computer because it doesn't turn on.

senses.definition: To notice or pay attention to a small detail.

examples.text: No reparé en su cambio de actitud hasta tarde.
examples.translation: I didn't notice his change in attitude until late.

faults.why: Missing the ser/estar split: es rico (wealthy) vs está rico (tasty).
Missing the everyday Mexican sense 'nice, lovely' (¡Qué rico se siente el sol!).

faults.quote: it can occasionally be used to mean 'cute' or 'attractive'
faults.why: Of a person, está rico means 'hot, sexy' and sounds flirtatious, not 'cute'.

notes: With ser it means wealthy (Es rico); with estar it means tasty or nice (¡Está rico!).
Said of a person with estar (está rico, está rica), it means 'attractive, hot', so it can sound flirtatious.

senses.definition: Having a lot of money, property, or valuable possessions.

examples.text: Ella trabaja mucho porque quiere ser rica.
examples.translation: She works a lot because she wants to be rich.

senses.definition: Having a very good flavor; delicious.

examples.text: ¡Qué rico está este pastel!
examples.translation: This cake is so delicious!

senses.definition: Pleasant to feel or experience.

examples.text: ¡Qué rico se siente el aire fresco!
examples.translation: The fresh air feels so nice!

faults.quote: The color of blood or a ripe tomato.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun.
Both notes restate agreement and the meaning; red wine (tinto) and red hair (pelirrojo) are the traps.

notes: Red wine is vino tinto, and red hair is pelirrojo (Es pelirroja, she has red hair), not rojo.
As a noun, the color is masculine: el rojo es mi color favorito.

senses.definition: Of the color of blood or a ripe tomato.

examples.text: Me compré una camisa roja.
examples.translation: I bought myself a red shirt.

examples.text: Se puso rojo de vergüenza.
examples.translation: He turned red with embarrassment.

faults.quote: Romper can mean breaking a physical object into pieces
faults.why: Restates the senses.
Missing the irregular participle roto and se me rompió.

faults.quote: Ellos decidieron romper su noviazgo
faults.why: Stiff; people say romper con alguien or just rompieron.

corrected.shortGloss: to break; to tear; to break up
notes: The past participle is irregular: roto (El vaso está roto, the glass is broken).
Se me rompió el vaso says that something broke on you, by accident, without saying you broke it.

senses.definition: To make something fall into pieces by force or impact.

examples.text: Voy a romper la piñata con un palo.
examples.translation: I am going to break the piñata with a stick.

senses.definition: To pull or damage material so that it splits or tears.

examples.text: El niño rompió la hoja sin querer.
examples.translation: The boy tore the page by accident.

senses.definition: To end a relationship with someone.

examples.text: Rompió con su novio la semana pasada.
examples.translation: She broke up with her boyfriend last week.

faults.quote: While 'ruidoso' can describe anything that makes sound
faults.why: Restates the definition.

notes: Do not confuse this with 'fuerte'. 'Fuerte' is used for the volume of a sound (like a loud voice), while 'ruidoso' refers to an object, place, or person that creates noise as an inherent quality.

senses.definition: Causing or producing a lot of noise.

examples.text: Los vecinos son muy ruidosos por la noche.
examples.translation: The neighbors are very noisy at night.

examples.text: Compré un ventilador menos ruidoso para mi oficina.
examples.translation: I bought a less noisy fan for my office.
